subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust/provenance contract should OpenClaw enforce for durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, session-memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but implementation requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, durable schema and migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and what belongs in native memory versus external plugins or MCP integrations.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

options.title: Split Provenance Foundation First
options.body: Make a durable provenance contract canonical first, then keep this issue for trust tiers, review gates, expiration, and trust-weighted retrieval.

options.title: Rely On External Integrations For Now
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp, AKF, Memory Wiki, and similar integrations as optional paths while intentionally leaving native OpenClaw memory without trust enforcement.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior review context on this issue and is the best available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
